  > 1. Derived PPI++ exactly: λ* = Cov(Y,f)/[Var(f)(1+n/N)], V = (Var(Y)/n)(1 − ρ²/(1+n/N)). The pooled estimator with best linear g has the *same* variance, because 1−n/M = 1/(1+n/N): PPI++ with tuned λ is the pooled linear estimator with λ = b*·N/M. So the "pooled Z" step is worth exactly zero over tuned PPI++ for linear g; the V_g(1/N−1/M) gain belongs to the PPI(λ=1) → PPI++ step. The decomposition is now classical → PPI → PPI++ → calibrated g → +X → floor, and "pooled linear" stays only as a numerical equality check. Exact excess of PPI++ over the floor: (1/n−1/M)·E(m−a*−b*f)². Please re-check this equivalence; it changes what I told you in the previous reply.
  > 2. Break-even stated in common units (excess in Var(h)); n* ≈ d_eff σ²_res/Δ·(K−1)/K for parametric calibrators, with an n_train^{-2/3}-type cost model for isotonic/trees.
  > 3. RRZ 1994 and Tsiatis 2006 cited for the "regular estimators cannot do better" half (not read in full; paper cites or proves).
  > 4. SE² = V̂ar(Y)/M + (1/n−1/M)V̂ar(h) with out-of-fold h, fold-model average on unlabeled records; validity for any L2-stable limit g_lim, assumptions listed.
